papers.title: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II
papers.abstract: We confirm a conjecture of the first author [SODA'26] on a strong form of pseudo-telepathy for Khot's $d$-to-$1$ games: for every $d\geq 4$, every $\epsilon>0$, and every $k\in\mathbb N$, there is a $d$-to-$1$ label-cover game of classical value less than $\epsilon$ that admits a perfect quantum strategy using finite-dimensional shared entanglement with measurement contexts of radius at least $k$. As a consequence, there exist graphs whose quantum chromatic number $\chi_q$ is $3$ and whose classical chromatic number $\chi$ is arbitrarily large. This is the first super-exponential $\chi_q$ vs. $\chi$ gap, and it improves on the exponential lower bounds of Brassard, Cleve, and Tapp [Phys. Rev. Lett. '99], who produced graphs for which $\chi\geq 1.1397^{\chi_q}$, and Lalonde, who recently achieved $\chi\geq 1.1546^{\chi_q}$. To prove the conjecture, we proceed as follows. We start with a ``stretched'' version of the Mermin-Peres magic square, obtained by spacing out its equations and linking them with additional long equation wires. This operation increases the radius of the initial measurement contexts of a perfect quantum strategy for the game, while preserving classical unsatisfiability. We then apply parallel repetition to make the classical value small, and we turn the system into a pseudo-telepathic multi-layered Kneser hypergraph via a PCP construction of Dinur, Guruswami, Khot, and Regev [STOC'03]. Finally, we feed the resulting hypergraph into the reduction of Fei, Minzer, and Wang from hypergraph colouring to $4$-to-$1$ games, we establish quantum completeness of this reduction, and we show that it preserves context radius.

papers.title: BMV conjecture and positivity of spectral shift for relatively Schatten perturbations
papers.abstract: We establish BMV-type results and prove the positivity-preserving property and uniqueness of support-normalized spectral shift functions of arbitrary order for semibounded operators with relatively Schatten-von Neumann perturbations. We also derive correlation inequalities in the relative Hilbert-Schmidt case. These results build on a new positivity-preserving property for the trace of a higher-order operator derivative along a relatively Schatten direction and are obtained using methods of multilinear operator integration and approximation.

papers.title: Linear maps of $C^*$-algebras preserving norm parallelism
papers.abstract: Two elements $a,b$ in a normed space are parallel if $\|a+\gamma b\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$ for some $|\gamma|=1$; they form a triangle equality attaining (TEA) pair if $\|a+b\|=\|a\|+\|b\|$. For finite-dimensional complex $C^*$-algebras other than $\mathbf M_2(\mathbb C)$ and $\mathbb C\oplus_\infty\mathbb C$, bijective linear maps on these algebras preserving parallel or TEA pairs are scalar multiples of isometries. For unital abelian algebras with spectra containing at least three points, preservation in both directions gives the same conclusion. We obtain corresponding results for type I factors, simple type I $C^*$-algebras, and unitarily invariant operator spaces under additional continuity and finite-rank hypotheses. All results for $C(X)$ and $B(H,K)$ hold over both real and complex fields.

papers.title: Independent Backward Preimages and Algebraic Radial Decompositions of Operators
papers.abstract: Let $T\in\mathcal{B}(X)$, where $X$ is a complex Banach space. We introduce the spaces $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$, defined by independently chosen preimages under the powers of $T$ with exponential growth bounds, and study algebraic radial decompositions involving $\mathcal{H}_r(T)$, $\mathcal{K}_s(T)$, and $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$. We prove that every algebraic decomposition $X=\mathcal{H}_r(T)\oplus\mathcal{I}_s(T)$ is topological and that $\mathcal{I}_s(T)=\mathcal{K}_s(T)$. This removes the closedness assumption in the radial decomposition theorem of Koliha and Poon. We also prove that, for $0\leq a\leq b$, the closedness of $\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ and $\mathcal{H}_a(T)+\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ implies $\mathcal{I}_b(T)=\mathcal{K}_b(T)$. We establish finite-defect and circular spectral criteria and characterize the Cantor--Bendixson derivatives of the spectrum, Browder spectrum, and Drazin spectrum in terms of radial decompositions and quotient restrictions. As applications, we obtain new characterizations of generalized Drazin, generalized Drazin--Riesz, generalized Drazin--meromorphic, and $g_z$-invertible operators in terms of radial subspaces.

papers.title: Sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities for some locally compact quantum groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that the usual Hausdorff--Young inequalities for locally compact quantum groups such as the quantum \(E_q(2)\), the real quantum \(az+b\), and the extended quantum \(SU_q(1,1)\), where \(0<q<1\), are sharp. Moreover, there are no group-like projections with finite Haar weight in these locally compact quantum groups. We obtain a sharp Hausdorff--Young inequality for Kahng's skew-matrix quantum groups; the optimal constant is strictly less than one for \(1<p<2\); at \(p=2\), Plancherel gives equality, and these quantum groups have no nonzero group-like projections with finite Haar weight.

papers.title: Variational formulae for entropy-like functionals for states in von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: The paper presents variational formulae for entropy-like functionals, including Segal and R\'enyi entropies, for normal states on semifinite von Neumann algebras. The considered functionals are of the form $\tau(f(h))$ where $\tau$ is a normal faithful semifinite trace on this algebra, $h$ is a positive selfadjoint operator from $L^1(\mathscr{M},\tau)$, and $f$ is an appropriate convex or concave function. The results cover both finite and semifinite algebras, and the obtained formulae generalise known results, in particular, those concerning relative entropy. Moreover, the connection between quantum entropies and the structure of abelian subalgebras is highlighted, providing new interpretations in the context of quantum information theory.

papers.title: The Quantum Stochastic Limit for Non-Markovian Driving Processes
papers.abstract: We express the stochastic limit (weak-coupling limit) of a quantum system interacting with its environment as the limit of solutions to a parametrized family of quantum stochastic differential equations (QSDEs). We prove the convergence of such solutions in the case where the driving processes may be non-Markovian and the system may be infinite-dimensional with unbounded Hamiltonian. We achieve this by imposing a particular condition on the n-point functions of the driving process which we verify for annihilation, creation, and gauge operators on a bosonic Fock space with sufficient mixing. Additionally, we include not only the usual fast-evolving system Hamiltonian which is averaged out in the limit, but also a slow-evolving system Hamiltonian which survives the limit. We also relax the requirement for the fast-evolving Hamiltonian to have a purely discrete spectrum allowing accumulation points under some circumstances. Moreover, our convergence mode for the processes is convergence of all time-centered n-point functions which is stronger than the typical semigroup convergence for the stochastic limit.

papers.title: Pauli Supported Invariants for Periodic Graphs-Derived Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: We introduce a graph invariant obtained from Pauli decompositions of Hamiltonians derived from local graph neighborhoods. Given a rooted h-hop neighborhood, we construct a local adjacency operator, embed it into a common Hilbert space dimension, and define its Pauli-support set as the collection of Pauli strings appearing with nonzero coefficients. For periodic graphs, we prove invariance under lattice-compatible graph equivalence and establish converse results under root-separation hypothesis. The framework naturally extends to Lie closures, commutants, and Cartan-type structures generated by the associated Pauli supports. We further discuss extensions to aperiodic graphs with finite local complexity and make connections to cut-and-project models of quasicrystals and notably, Penrose tilings. From a quantum information perspective, the resulting invariants provide a operator-theoretic description of graph-based Hamiltonians and offer a new mechanism for comparing graph-based quantum systems through Pauli-support data.

papers.title: Hybrid Clifford Codes via Operator Algebra Quantum Error Correction and Projective Representation Theory
papers.abstract: Clifford codes are a natural generalization of quantum stabilizer codes based primarily on representation theory. This class of codes has previously been extended to the setting of quantum subsystem codes. We formulate a two-fold generalization of Clifford codes, for both the hybrid classical and quantum information and projective representation theory settings. This leads to new classes of hybrid subspace and subsystem Clifford codes. We extend the fundamental representation theoretic quantum error correction theorem to include these codes, based on the operator algebra quantum error correction framework. We also discuss several examples throughout the presentation, of both stabilizer and non-stabilizer type.

papers.title: Single commutators in Schatten ideals
papers.abstract: Let $r>2$ and let $p,q\in(0,\infty)$ satisfy $r^{-1}=p^{-1}+q^{-1}$. We prove that every $T\in \mathcal{S}_r(\mathcal H)$ is a single commutator $T=[A,B]$ with $A\in \mathcal{S}_p(\mathcal H)$ and $B\in \mathcal{S}_q(\mathcal H)$. Combined with L. G. Brown's theorem for $1 \leq r \leq 2$, this completely resolves the Pearcy--Topping problem for Schatten ideals. We also obtain simultaneous operator and Schatten norm bounds for the factors.

papers.title: Unital embeddings of the Jiang--Su algebra are not unique
papers.abstract: We show that the canonical embeddings of the Jiang--Su algebra $\mathcal Z$ into the universal unital free product $\mathcal Z \ast_{\mathbb C}\mathcal Z$ are not approximately unitarily equivalent. This answers a question appearing in one of the $99$ problems list of Schafhauser, Tikuisis, and White. By contrast, we prove that any two such embeddings into a selfless $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebra are strongly asymptotically unitarily equivalent.

papers.title: Factoriality of Mixed $q$-Gaussian Algebras at the Boundary
papers.abstract: For arbitrary index set $I$, we determine the center and characterize factoriality for mixed $q$-Gaussian von Neumann algebras $\Gamma_Q(\cH_\R)$ associated with real symmetric matrices $Q=(q_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ satisfying $|q_{ij}|\le1$ through the strict graph we introduced in this article. Two vertices $i$ and $j$ of $I$ are joined by an edge in the strict graph if and only if $|q_{ij}|<1$. Let $S$ denote its isolated vertices. We prove that $\Gamma_Q(\cH_\R)$ is a factor if and only if $q_{ii}=-1$ for every $i\in S$, no two-vertex component $\{a,b\}$ satisfies $q_{aa}=q_{bb}=-1$, and no nonempty finite subset $A\subseteq S$ satisfies $\prod_{j\in A\setminus \{k\}}q_{jk}=1$ for every $k\in I$. We also determine the laws of some central elements.
